program: pre-registration literature survey for the programmatic-primitives + hybrid router idea (12 Aug 2026)

registration_notes.N88.1: This is a SURVEY for a new, unsealed engineering idea - not a claim audit. Nothing here can promote or withdraw a sealed claim.
registration_notes.N88.2: Question registered before search: could a GEODE-style system treat well-defined computations (math, shape checks, known transforms) as PROGRAMMATIC primitives with the same fingerprint interface as learned primitives, and route through them with a planner/controller - keeping a learned model only for fingerprinting, open-goal routing, and tasks with no programmatic primitive - to win on footprint and energy at modest accuracy cost?
registration_notes.N88.3: Anchors are recall probes: each MUST be retrieved by a topic query that does NOT contain its title, else the search is insensitive and every 'not found' is worthless.
registration_notes.N88.4: Query families are phrased to find displacing work (work that already builds programmatic+learned hybrids, tool-augmented models, learned routers with fallback, or solves the interface-contract problem), not work that merely agrees in spirit.
registration_notes.N88.5: Empty queries are recorded, not dropped. Rate-limited queries are retried and residual failures recorded separately from genuinely empty results.
registration_notes.N88.6: Absence from these indexes is UNRESOLVED, never 'new' or 'first'. Unauthenticated public search cannot support a novelty claim.
registration_notes.N88.7: Title/abstract mark a source live; only primary text with a located passage may count as displacement.
registration_notes.N88.8: This evidence is a dated snapshot and is NOT replayable: the indexes change and the network is not a sealed corpus. The run records its date and the exact query strings so a reader can repeat the search, not so the bytes can be reproduced.
registration_notes.N88.9: Instrument reused from M127 (audit_v13_prior_art): arXiv two-stage AND-then-OR, Semantic Scholar with retry; S2 rate-limiting recorded as failures, not empty.

anchors: language model learning to use tools
large language model connected to APIs

D1.statement: Programmatic computation is already served to a learned model as an external tool (calculator / code interpreter / function call), with the model deciding when to invoke it.
queries: large language model external tool use
language model tool augmentation arithmetic accuracy
toolformer teach language model use tools

D2.statement: Hybrid neuro-symbolic systems already compose learned models with programmatic/symbolic modules in one pipeline.
queries: symbolic program neural network hybrid system

D3.statement: The interface-contract problem (typed input/output schema between a learned module and a programmatic tool) is already addressed in the literature.
queries: function calling schema generation large language model
typed interface tool specification language model
structured input output contract neural module

D4.statement: A planner/controller (LLM or symbolic) already selects among a library of modules/tools toward an open goal, including for non-LLM downstream modules.
queries: language model planner select module task
LLM controller orchestrate multiple tools goal
goal directed module selection agent planning
LLM tool selection planning open goal
agent skill composition task planning controller

D5.statement: Fallback/abstention/cascade techniques already handle the case where the selected module is wrong or out of contract.

D6.statement: Energy/footprint-aware routing or sparse dispatch already exists as a measured design goal for learned systems.
queries: energy efficient mixture of experts routing
edge deployment sparse routing tiny model
low power on device machine learning routing

D7.statement: Skill/primitive libraries with a task planner already exist (robotics/agents) as a reusable pattern for programmatic + learned composition.

D8.statement: Program synthesis / DSL / code-as-primitive is already used to turn spec into executable programmatic modules for a learned system.
